question: Exclusion of producers from the application of Measure 23 and critical liquidity support, with serious financial and operational consequences

Farmers who suffered documented losses exceeding 30 % of their production, but were nevertheless excluded from Measure 23, face serious and immediate financial and operational consequences. The purpose of the measure was to alleviate ‘liquidity difficulties’ and mitigate ‘income reduction’ caused by natural disasters.

Without access to this emergency support, farmers are forced to shoulder the burden of significant production losses. This precarious situation can lead to a chain of negative consequences, including increased debt, reduced capacity to invest and, in extreme cases, the forced cessation of their agricultural activities.

The fact that severely affected farmers, such as the pistachio producers of Phthiotis, are excluded from critical liquidity support does not simply represent a missed opportunity for individual assistance, but directly exacerbates their pre-existing financial vulnerability.

When a programme explicitly designed to function as a safety net demonstrably fails to reach a significant proportion of its intended beneficiaries, it inevitably creates deep disappointment and distrust.

Repeated failures to provide the promised and necessary assistance erode trust and highlight the Government’s inability to respond effectively to crisis management, which hinders the development and implementation of long-term climate change adaptation and agricultural sustainability strategies. Can the Commission respond to the following: 1.
Why were areas and crops excluded from the implementation of the Measure?
Can it be amended?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (23.10.

2025) When planning the exceptional temporary support to farmers, forest holders and Small and Medium Enterprises, particularly affected by natural disasters, provided in accordance with Article 6a of Regulation (EU) 2020/22201 (so called Measure 23) the Member States were required to target the support to beneficiaries who were most affected by natural disasters, by determining eligibility conditions on the basis of available evidence (paragraph 4 of that Article).

This was to ensure that the support would be for the benefit of the farmers who had suffered the most, also taking into account the limited available resources. The targeting of the support and its justification has been included in the relevant Rural Development Programme (RDP) and approved by the Commission.

As different types of natural disasters have occurred across Europe, and as the structure and characteristics of the agricultural sector vary between the Member States, the groups of beneficiaries who were most affected by natural disasters, identified by the Member States as recipients of the aid granted under Measure 23, may vary as well.

As laid down in paragraph 5 of Article 6a, the support has to be paid by 31 December 2025, based on applications for support approved by the competent authority by 30 June 2025. It is therefore not possible to change the targeting of the support or approve new applications for support now.
